title: What to Expect From Moody's Q3 2025 Earnings Report
content: Moody's Corporation (MCO), a New York-based integrated risk assessment firm with a market cap of $87.4 billion, is expected to report its fiscal third-quarter 2025 earnings before the market opens on Wednesday, October 22, 2025. Analysts forecast diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.51, a 9.4% increase from $3.21 in the same quarter of 2024. The company has exceeded Wall Street's EPS estimates in its last four consecutive quarters. For the full fiscal year 2025, analysts expect EPS of $13.92, up 11.6% from $12.47 in fiscal 2024, with a projected rise to $15.64 in fiscal 2026, a 12.4% year-over-year increase. MCO stock has underperformed both the S&P 500 Index's 17.4% gain and the Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund's (XLF) 18% gain over the past 52 weeks, with shares rising only 4.1% during that period. On July 23, 2025, MCO shares rose over 1% after reporting Q2 results, with revenue reaching $1.9 billion, up 4.5% year over year, and adjusted EPS increasing 8.5% to $3.56. Analysts' consensus rating is 'Moderate Buy,' with 13 out of 25 analysts issuing a 'Strong Buy,' 10 maintaining a 'Hold,' one advising a 'Moderate Buy,' and one recommending a 'Strong Sell.' The average analyst price target is $542.19, implying a 10.6% potential upside from current levels.

Steele selling 1,457 shares, decreasing his ownership by 51.25%. In total, insiders sold 9,423 shares valued at $4.81 million over the past three months. Institutional investors own 92.11% of the company’s stock, with recent purchases by Rexford Capital Inc., Newbridge Financial Services Group Inc., Johnson Financial Group Inc., Saudi Central Bank, and Wolff Wiese Magana LLC (which increased its stake by 1,000%). title: 14 Analysts Assess Moodys: What You Need To Know - Moodys (NYSE:MCO)
content: Over the past three months, 14 analysts have provided assessments of Moody's (NYSE:MCO), offering a range of views from bullish to bearish. The average 12-month price target for Moody's stock is $557.79, up 3.46% from the previous average of $539.15, with individual estimates ranging from a low of $528.00 to a high of $597.00. Analysts have adjusted their ratings, with actions including 'Maintain', 'Raise', and 'Lower', reflecting evolving perceptions based on company performance and market conditions. Ratings span from 'Outperform' to 'Underperform', indicating expectations for relative stock performance. title: Moody's prevé asignar una calificación 'Ba2' a la nueva emisión de bonos de Gestamp
content: Moody’s forecasts a rating of 'Ba2' for Gestamp’s new bond issue, matching the company’s long‑term corporate rating of 'Ba2' with a stable outlook. The new bonds will fund the refinancing of €400 million of senior secured bonds maturing in April 2026, €83 million of Schuldschein notes due in 2026, and cover transaction costs and general corporate purposes. Moody’s notes that the transaction will improve liquidity by extending the group’s debt maturity profile to 2030. Gestamp’s leverage, measured as adjusted gross debt over EBITDA, has remained steady at 3.8× in the twelve months to June 2025, close to the 3.75× threshold for a 'Ba2' rating, up from 3.6× at the end of 2024. The 3.8× figure reflects a €63 million decline in adjusted EBITDA in the first half of 2025, largely due to foreign‑exchange losses, hyperinflationary effects, and €9.5 million extraordinary costs linked to the 'Phoenix' restructuring plan in NAFTA. Excluding those costs, EBITDA was essentially flat, with the margin improving to 11.1% from 10.6% a year earlier. Moody’s expects that the new bonds may carry a higher coupon than the debt they refinance, slightly raising financing costs, reducing interest coverage, and producing a modestly negative adjusted free‑cash‑flow after dividends over the next 12–18 months. Nevertheless, the retained cash‑flow‑to‑net‑debt ratio of 23.7% (June 2025) remains within the 20–25% range for a 'Ba2' rating and should strengthen after the announced transaction with Banco Santander, which injected €246 million for a 38.6% stake in a new Spanish real‑estate holding of Gestamp. The new bonds, like the debt they refinance, will be secured by subsidiaries that account for about 45% of consolidated EBITDA and by a first lien on shares of six Spanish sub‑holdings that hold the core business.

title: Moody's, Newmont'un notunu A3'e yükseltti, görünümü stabil Yazar Investing.com
content: Moody's Ratings upgraded Newmont Corporation's first‑degree unsecured bond rating from Baa1 to A3 and changed the outlook from positive to stable, citing significant improvements in the company’s credit profile.  Senior Credit Officer and Newmont’s chief analyst Botir Sharipov explained that 'Güçlü kredi metrikleri, mükemmel likidite ve muhafazakar mali politikalara bağlılık bu kararın temelini oluşturuyor.'  Newmont reduced its gross debt by roughly 3.9 billion dollars between 2024 and 2025, driven by $3.1 billion of after‑tax cash from asset sales in 2025 and $700 million from 2024 sales.  The company paid $483 million of debt in 2024 and $1.4 billion in the first half of 2025, and completed $2 billion of bond buy‑backs in Q3 2025.  Moody's adjusted debt/EBITDA ratio fell to 0.7× as of 30 June 2025 from 1× at the end of 2024 and 2.6× at the end of 2023, while the adjusted EBITDA margin rose to about 42% from 33% and 14% in prior periods.  Newmont adopted a new dividend policy in 2024, setting annual dividends at $1 per share (≈$1.1 billion) and increased its share‑repurchase program to $6 billion, completing $2.8 billion of buy‑backs between February 2024 and 24 July 2025.  With $6.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $4 billion of unused revolving credit as of 30 June 2025, Moody's forecasts adjusted EBITDA of $9.6‑9.7 billion for 2025 and a leverage ratio of 0.6× by year‑end, assuming gold prices of $2,900 per ounce.  The stable outlook reflects Moody's view that Newmont will maintain a steady production profile, focus on cost improvements, and adhere to disciplined capital‑allocation strategies to preserve A3‑level credit metrics.

title: Will Moody's Robust 1H25 Revenue and Earnings Growth Continue?
content: Moody's Corp. reported strong first-half 2025 results, with $3.82 billion in revenues and earnings per share of $6.66, representing year-over-year growth of 6.1% and 8.1%, respectively. The growth was partly driven by the January acquisition of CAPE Analytics. In the second quarter alone, total revenues reached $1.9 billion, with $1.01 billion from the Moody's Analytics division. Annualized recurring revenue (ARR) for Moody's Analytics was $3.3 billion, up 8.1% year-over-year, led by Decision Solutions. Recurring and transaction revenues for Moody's Investors Service accounted for 67% of segment revenues in the first half of 2025, down 100 basis points from the prior year, primarily due to growth in Corporate Finance revenues driven by investment-grade issuers. Moody's operating margin was 43.5%, down 20 basis points from the prior year due to higher restructuring and depreciation/amortization charges. The company has achieved over $100 million in annualized savings from its efficiency program, which is expected to continue delivering benefits. Management projects 2025 earnings per share to be between $12.25 and $12.75, narrowing the previous range of $12.00–$12.75. While the first-half growth was driven by a favorable issuance mix and a broad product suite, sustainability depends on capitalizing on high-growth regions and strategic collaborations. The article also notes strong performance from MSCI Inc. (9.4% revenue growth) and S&P Global Inc. (7% net revenue growth), though market dynamics may affect future demand. The piece concludes with a promotional note on AI-driven investment opportunities, highlighting 'AI Boom 2.0' and four under-the-radar companies poised for growth.

title: Moody's sees stable credit quality across Mexico, Brazil, Argentina through 2026
content: Moody's has projected that Latin American corporate credit profiles will remain stable through at least 2026, despite global trade tensions and regional political uncertainty. The outlook varies by economy but generally shows no significant deterioration expected over the next two years. For Brazil, Moody's expects corporate credit quality to hold steady through 2026, citing that "three-quarters" of the country's rated debt is held by commodity exporters and that lower inflation expectations for 2026 help moderate risks while direct impact from U.S. trade tensions remains limited. Mexico is expected to maintain corporate and infrastructure credit stability with improving metrics, though investor caution remains over uncertain U.S. trade terms and global tariff effects; Moody's notes that falling foreign direct investment reflects hesitation regarding recent regulatory and legal changes. Argentina’s corporate, infrastructure and regional government credit quality should continue improving through 2026, supported by macroeconomic stabilisation and increased credit access following a late‑2024 recovery, though institutional fragility, limited capital account opening and weak external buffers remain vulnerabilities. Colombia maintains a stable outlook despite political uncertainty ahead of May 2026 elections, with the oil and gas industry avoiding significant stress through mature reserve partnerships and national companies benefiting from favourable credit environments. Chile’s corporate credit remains broadly stable alongside a moderate economic recovery, with GDP projected above 2% in 2025‑2026; consumer‑linked sectors will drive growth while exporters face Chinese economic exposure. Peru maintains solid corporate and infrastructure credit profiles with positive free cash flow expected, supported by flexible regulations and cost advantages despite investor caution before April 2026 presidential elections.

title: 惠譽確認美國評級為AA+ 展望穩定
content: Moody’s has confirmed the United States’ long‑term foreign‑currency issuer default rating (IDR) at 'AA+' with a stable outlook. The agency projects that the federal government’s budget deficit will shrink from 7.7% of GDP last year to 6.9% this year, driven by a significant rise in revenue. Revenue growth is attributed to resilient economic expansion, solid equity market performance, and a sharp increase in tariff receipts. Moody’s estimates that the effective tariff rate rose from 2.3% at the end of last year to 16% by August, implying tariff revenue of about $250 billion—0.8% of GDP—well above the $77 billion forecast for 2024.

title: Moody's eleva la calificación de Five Point a B2 y asigna B2 a nuevos bonos Por Investing.com
content: Moody's Ratings raised Five Point Holdings' corporate family rating from 'B3' to 'B2', keeping the outlook stable. The agency also assigned a 'B2' rating to the proposed $450 million senior unsecured notes due 2030. The upgrade reflects a 28 % debt reduction since the end of 2023, with leverage expected to stay around 16 % debt-to-book‑capital through 2026. Proceeds will be used to redeem existing senior unsecured notes of $1.5 million due 2025 and $523.5 million due 2028, after which those bonds will be delisted. The transaction reduces refinancing risk and extends the company’s maturity profile; the only remaining maturity in the next five years is a $100 million senior unsecured revolving credit line due July 2027. Despite the upgrade, Five Point’s 'B2' rating remains constrained by its small scale—$200 million annual revenue and heavy reliance on the Great Park Venture in Irvine, California. Key credit strengths include low leverage and no short‑term maturities; non‑consolidated entity distributions are expected to cover annual cash interest payments of about $40 million, below the $55 million paid in 2024. The company holds $457 million in cash as of June 30 2025 and full access to a $125 million revolving credit line. Its unencumbered land portfolio was book‑valued at $2.4 billion on that date. Moody’s said a rating improvement could occur if the firm expands scale and diversification while keeping debt‑to‑capital below 25 %; a downgrade could happen if debt‑to‑capital exceeds 30 % or operating performance deteriorates.
